newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals ranged on low demand, world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals ranged on low demand, world trend.

text.p: Base metals were steady in a narrow price band on local markets, dealers said on Monday.

Demand from industrial consumers was at low ebb but limited arrivals and narrow fluctuations in world market depressed local prices. Tin was steady at 31,200 rupees per quintal after losing 300 rupees last week.
Zinc was steady at 7,650 rupees as was lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal, with the market consolidating recent gains. Last week zinc was up 150 rupees and lead by 25 rupees per quintal.
Copper, aluminium and nickel finished on a quiet note amid limited activity.
Copper was steady at 13,400 rupees while aluminium was quiet at 7,400 rupees and nickel at 37,300 rupees per quintal.
Copper was up by 50 rupees per quintal last week.
Overall sentiments was subdued at the close amid limited physical enquiries and strigent monetary conditions.
